cur:monumental-san-sheep-and-goats.summary: Christ, young and beardless in a purple robe, sits enthroned between two angels: a red-clad angel stands beside the sheep at his right hand, a blue-clad angel beside the goats at his left. The image turns the parable of the Last Judgement into a calm, symmetrical vision of Christ as judge and shepherd, one of the earliest monumental images of the judgement in Christian art.
facts: Because the angel beside the goats is clothed in blue, some art historians have identified him as the earliest depiction of Satan (or a fallen angel) in Western art, though this reading is debated.
The thirteen scenes of the north wall show Christ's miracles and teaching; in all of them he appears young and beardless, robed in imperial purple.
The scenes were not arranged in biblical order but are thought to follow the Gospel readings of the Lenten liturgy in Theodoric's palace church.
